title: Rule or Model?
instruction: Should this be a hard business rule, or something the model learns?

items.why: A hard constraint: the model can't be trusted to learn it from clicks, and one miss costs a sale.

items.text: People who buy a tent often buy a sleeping pad next
items.why: A pattern in behaviour: exactly what models learn.

items.text: Don't recommend alcohol to users under the legal age
items.why: A legal requirement must never be violated, however rare the case.

items.text: This customer prefers trail shoes to road shoes
items.why: A personal preference, visible in their behaviour.

items.text: This series may only be shown in countries where it is licensed
items.why: Licensing is a contract, not a prediction.

items.text: Pin the spring campaign item to slot 1 this week
items.why: A strategic decision, not a relevance prediction.

items.text: Evening visitors click more on long reads
items.why: A context pattern the model can pick up from data.

items.text: Show at most 2 items from the same brand in the top 10
items.why: A diversity constraint applied in re-ranking.

items.text: Rank new arrivals by how likely this user is to click them
items.why: Relevance ranking is the model's job.

debrief: Algorithms optimize relevance. Rules enforce what the model can't know or must never get wrong: inventory, law, licensing, strategy.
